idea-plugin.name: Ruby Anonymous FQN Burst Guard
idea-plugin.description:
This plugin modifies RubyMine's behaviour at runtime. It stops Ruby code analysis from hanging forever on files that reference ActiveRecord models.

The defect. AnonymousDefiningCallType.getAnonymousClassName derives an anonymous class/module's fully-qualified name from (textRange.hashCode() << 15) ^ text.hashCode() alone. The containing file is not part of the identity, so every file whose anonymous defining call has identical text at an identical offset — several monkeypatch files each opening with ActiveRecord::Base.class_eval do, say — collapses into one symbol.

That merged symbol then resolves to every colliding declaration. SymbolHierarchy.getAncestorsFromAnonymousDefiningCalls looks the FQN up and re-enters ancestor resolution once per element returned, and nothing along the way can be memoized because RecursionManager holds the stack stamp for the duration of the cycle. Eleven colliding files, roughly thirteen levels deep, is not a slow computation — it is one that does not finish. A measured stall spent 33.7 million index lookups on a single key.

The fix. When one anonymous FQN is requested past a threshold on one thread with no pause, its stub-index lookup is served empty. An empty lookup empties the caller's element loop, so nothing is expanded and the recursion ends. Restricted to synthesized $$ANON FQNs, so ordinary constant resolution is untouched.

Trade-off: a cut lookup means an anonymous class's ancestor list can come back incomplete. Tunable, and disableable, via VM options:

  • -Drubyprobe.disabled=true — turn the patch off entirely
  • -Drubyprobe.burstMax=512 — lookups of one key, per thread, per burst
  • -Drubyprobe.burstQuietMillis=250 — pause that ends a burst

The first time the guard engages it logs one line to idea.log, tagged rubyprobe.
